description:
Move the `getContext` call out of `_createContext` and into `InternalRenderTask#initializeGraphics` and adapt tests accordingly.

This is a precursor to moving the call into a worker thread to let us use `OffscreenCanvas`. The current position wouldn't work since we make transformations to the canvas object after the `getContext` call, which isn't allowed for `OffscreenCanvas`. Also it isn't allowed to clone or `transferControlToOffscreen` the canvas after the `getContext` call.

comments.body: Is `#enableHWA` on this class still used for anything ,or can we completely remove it?
Great call, it is indeed not used anymore so I'll remove it from this class.

Isn't this an API-breaking change? If so, this patch should either be labeled as `[api-minor]` with a working fallback and deprecation warning, or as `[api-major]` if no sensible fallback can be used here.
nit: it could be an OffscreenCanvas too, right ?

In theory, yes. At the moment there's two main parts of the lifecycle of the canvas. There's a part where changes are made assuming an `HTMLCanvasElement`, in this part we're still passing an element. Later on (in a separate patch) the canvas is transferred into an `OffscreenCanvas` and now I'm working on dispatching operations that can be made on that to the worker (since the canvas is no longer owned by the main thread).

It was indeed, which is also why we had all the test breakage. I think with my latest update now some of the test changes can indeed be reverted if you prefer I do that. That said, I made a change that would allow the change to not be breaking (set the default value of `canvas` to `canvasContext.canvas` and continue to accept `canvasContext`).

We should indicate the replacement option here so that users know what to migrate towards. I would suggest "canvasContext - Deprecated 2D context of a DOM Canvas object for backwards compatibility; use the `canvas` parameter instead."

"canvas - A DOM Canvas object. The default value is the canvas associated with the `canvasContext` parameter if no value is provided explicitly." (fixes the `paramter` typo and makes it a bit easier to read)
Can we make `this.enableHWA` private here (so `this._enableHWA`) too to limit the API surface, or is it used in the public API somewhere?
Let's add a new test that deliberately uses the legacy `canvasContext` to keep coverage for it until it's eventually removed, to avoid regressions in that code path.
I think this can be removed now that `InternalRenderTask` seems to no longer use this given that this patch switched it to use `canvas` instead?
It's not entirely clear to me why this member variable, and the constructor change, is necessary given that I can't find a place where this is read. What am I missing here?
This no longer depends on `enableHWA`; is that expected?

https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/pull/20016/files/0fec688be8f3560e3e64d6d02947f78d9442f151#diff-bbfa425a29357467994ff26c711a1818a6b8bd7774176822e042a971f4e71addL381 the original call was passing `true` to `enableHWA` so in this path it was always evaluating to `willReadFrequently: false`.
Good point; thanks for the clarification!

However, it looks like `enableHWA` in this file is now unused, so can we remove all references to it to simplify things further? AFAICT we currently still set e.g. `this.enableHWA` even though nothing seems to read from it anymore.
Thanks, got rid of it now.

So it's needed atm in `InternalRenderTask` in order to make the necessary `getContext` call and since that's called by `PDFPageProxy#render`, I'm storing it on `WorkerTransport` in order to pass it on here: https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/pull/20016/files#diff-082d6b37ad01db7ac97cc07c6ddb0dc52040484c5ef91b110b072f50144d9f39R1520.

In my follow-on PR (already up but in draft state at #20053), you would notice that the `getContext` call moves to a worker thread where I set `enableHWA` at the beginning once so I'll remove it from `WorkerTransport` as part of that patch.

I went around checking the flow of that info and realized it was needed atleast until we want to make the `getContext` call in `InternalRenderTask` due to the clarification in https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/pull/20016#discussion_r2181079795.
Nevermind my last comment, I misunderstood you at first. I removed `enableHWA` from `PDFThumbnailView`.

Linting currently fails on this because using `waitForTimeout` is discouraged as it often introduced intermittent failures, so deterministic methods should be used instead of fixed timeouts.

In this case it would be better to, for example, wait for the `data-loaded="true"` attribute to be present on the `thumbnail` class instead because that is an indicator that loading finished.

It's not really clear to me why the `currentScaleValue` is changed here because AFAICT  changing the zoom level doesn't change the thumbnails (I tried in the viewer just now). I tried running this line in the web console of the viewer and it zooms to 5000% which is probably also not what you meant to do here.

What does change the thumbnails is rotating the page for example, so you could do that to trigger a re-rendering of the thumbnails.

What would be a good order of assertions before _and_ after the re-rendering is:

- Wait for `thumbSelector` to be visible (you already have this).
- Wait for the `data-loaded="true"` attribute to appear on `thumbnail` as an indicator that loading finished.
- Check if `src="data:image" is present (you already have this).
- Ideally, if feasible with the data URL, check if the image content contains non-zero pixels like you already made for the `should work with the legacy canvasContext parameter` test.
Thanks for the suggestion, it worked like a charm.
Okay with the last change this is the only remaining thing to do.

I'm also fine with the current version if the last step is not easy to do. The most important goal of this test, which is to check that the basic thumbnail rendering flow works, seems satisfied by the this test now.
